overall_diagnosis: All three samples agree: the baseline agent failed Steps 2 and 3 of the Reserves-at-Risk task by applying an extra √3 horizon-scaling factor to an already-3-month volatility. The agent used `reserves × Z × σ_3m × √3 / 100` instead of the correct `reserves × Z × σ_3m / 100`, inflating all Step 2 gold valuation exposures and Step 3 RaR% values by ~1.732×. This error cascades from Step 2 to Step 3. The only available skill is the generic xlsx skill, which lacks domain guidance on VaR-style shock calculations and horizon-matched volatility conventions. Augmenting it with a Reserves-at-Risk methodology note is the sole repair lever.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill covers generic spreadsheet formatting, formula hygiene, and color coding, but offers no domain-specific guidance for financial risk calculations such as Reserves-at-Risk (RaR) or 95% one-sided value-at-risk shocks. The agent double-scaled the volatility by multiplying an already-3-month σ by √3, inflating Step 2 exposures and Step 3 RaR% by ~√3 ≈ 1.732. The skill lacks any warning against this common VaR horizon double-scaling mistake, nor does it clarify handling of countries missing 2025 data.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a 'Financial risk / VaR calculations' subsection under Financial models with the following guidance: (1) When a volatility is already measured over the target horizon (e.g., σ_3m computed as STDEV of the last 3 monthly log-returns×100), it represents a horizon-matched shock in percent and must NOT be further multiplied by √horizon. The correct one-sided 95% shock is `Exposure = Value × 1.645 × σ_period / 100` with NO additional √T factor. (2) Only apply √T scaling when converting a shorter-period volatility to a longer horizon (e.g., annualizing a monthly vol by √12). (3) For Reserves-at-Risk: `RaR% = Exposure / TotalReserves × 100`, computed from the horizon-matched exposure. (4) For countries present in the Volume sheet with 2025 data but missing from the Value sheet, convert using the Jan–Sep 2025 average gold price. (5) Drop any country lacking 2025 Total Reserves before computing Step 3 RaR. (6) Include a worked micro-example contrasting correct vs. incorrect use of √T to reinforce the convention.
